summary: The WorkAdmissionPort implementation for PgWorkStore: submit/cancel/accept/resume delegate to their transaction modules; policy_identity and policy_drifted are implemented here (the identity-catalog pair).
responsibilities: submit/cancel/accept/resume call require_project, then delegate: submit -> work_admission_submit::submit, cancel -> work_admission_ops::cancel, accept -> work_admission_ops::accept, resume -> work_admission_resume::resume.

policy_identity runs in one transaction: check readiness with SELECT to_regprocedure('forge_agent.coding_identity_register(text,text,text,text,jsonb,text)') IS NOT NULL AS ready; not ready -> rejected(503, identity_unavailable) (Python returns None pre-M44; the Rust port type has no None, documented divergence). Ready: document = the snapshot object minus its policy_digest key; call SELECT identity_id, generation FROM forge_agent.coding_identity_register($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6) with (owner, project_alias, kind, "policy", document, snapshot.policy_digest as text). Return PolicyIdentity { kind: kind.to_string(), digest: the snapshot's policy_digest } (the registration side effect is the operation's substance; identity_id/generation surface when the forge-work type grows). A snapshot without a policy_digest string -> rejected(400, invalid_request).

policy_drifted runs in one transaction: not ready -> Ok(false); run the workflow_policy_document query pinned in the pattern; no row -> Ok(false); else Ok(row.document != snapshot-minus-policy_digest). (Python returns None for the no-identity cases; the Rust bool maps None to false, documented.)
invariants: Delegation methods contain no SQL. The policy pair contains only the pinned SQL.
pattern:
// workflow_policy_document (forge_pg_proxy READ_QUERIES, verbatim with $n params):
// SELECT c.document FROM forge_agent.coding_task_identities i JOIN forge_agent.coding_identity_catalog c ON c.identity_id = i.workflow_policy_id WHERE i.owner_id = $1 AND i.workflow_id = $2 ORDER BY i.created_at LIMIT 1
